links.tooltip: Open the Alatyr policy graph in a new tab

panels.title: Evaluation freshness
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful full-cluster evaluation. Everything else on this dashboard is only true if this is green — read this panel first.

panels.title: Workloads (denominator)
panels.description: Total workloads observed. Every ratio below is over this number.

panels.title: Unpoliced
panels.description: Workloads no engine selects — default-open. Value + delta vs 24h ago. RED at 1: any workload uncovered by every engine is default-open, so any non-zero value is a finding.

panels.title: Internet-full (ingress + egress)
panels.description: Workloads reachable both ways from the internet — critical severity. RED at 1.

targets.expr: (sum(alatyr_workloads_internet_reachable{direction="both",namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}) or vector(0)) - (sum(alatyr_workloads_internet_reachable{direction="both",namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"} offset 24h) or vector(0))

panels.title: Internet-ingress
panels.description: Workloads reachable from the internet. RED at 1.

panels.title: Internet-egress
panels.description: Workloads permitted to reach the internet. YELLOW at 1.

panels.title: HBONE blocked
panels.description: Ambient workloads whose policy strips port 15008 — silent traffic loss. RED at 1.

panels.title: Single-engine coverage
panels.description: Share of workloads covered by exactly one engine — a silent-failure risk since the intersection collapses to that engine's opinion alone. YELLOW at any, RED >20%.

panels.title: Per-engine coverage rate
panels.description: Fraction of workloads each engine selects. An engine at 0% is either disabled or broken — cross-check the Freshness section. Per-engine, not intersected: a workload uncovered by engine X but covered by engine Y is not a gap unless engine X is expected to select it.

targets.expr: sum by (engine) (alatyr_workloads_covered{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}) / scalar(clamp_min(sum(alatyr_workloads{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}), 1)) or (max by (engine) (alatyr_engine_enabled) * 0)

panels.title: Workloads by status
panels.description: Effective status keys over time. Colors approximate the severity buckets in policy/catalog.go — internet-* red, lan-* orange, ns-* blue, air-gapped green, l7-applied teal.

panels.title: Status headline (current vs 24h)
panels.description: Every status key with its current cluster-wide count and its 24h delta. Auditors want deltas, not raw totals.

panels.title: Issues — counts are per (workload, engine) pair, not distinct problems
Issues by type (24h)
panels.description: Current issue counts by type over the last day. Control-plane namespaces are excluded by default (see $hide_infra template variable) — clear the variable to include them.

panels.title: Issue drill-down (namespace × type)
panels.description: Counts here are per (workload, engine) — a single conflict between two engines shows as 2.

panels.title: Namespaces partially enrolled
panels.description: Enrolled namespaces containing at least one opted-out workload. The rollout footgun as a single number.

panels.title: mTLS mode (cluster)
panels.description: Enrolled workloads by resolved mTLS verdict (strict/permissive/disabled/unset/unknown). `unknown` = PA fetch failed; alertable.

panels.title: Engine last success (age)
panels.description: Per-engine seconds since last successful evaluation. One engine failing while others succeed is the case the product is otherwise silent about.

panels.title: Evaluation duration (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Full-cycle wall-clock time. Drives the 'is the refresh interval sustainable' question.

panels.title: Engine evaluation duration p95
panels.description: Per-engine tail latency — pinpoints which engine dominates cycle time.

panels.title: Engine errors (rate)
panels.description: Bucketed engine failure rate. 'or vector(0)' forces a zero line so an empty result renders as 'no errors', not 'exporter down' — freshness (top row) is the definitive down-detector.

panels.title: Namespace scorecard
panels.description: One row per namespace. workloads = denominator; internet-full = worst-case reachability; unpoliced = zero engines select this workload; single-engine = only one engine covers it (intersection collapses to that engine's opinion); issues + policies = raw counts. Sorted by internet-full desc — the row a CISO reads first. `sum by (namespace)` is safe on all series here: none are engine-labelled, so no per-engine overcount.

panels.title: Per-namespace × engine coverage
panels.description: Fraction of workloads each engine selects, per namespace. `group_left` joins by namespace so the engine-labelled numerator can divide by the un-labelled workload total. Zero rows for a namespace means no engine touches it — cross-check the scorecard's `unpoliced` column. NOT summable across engines (a workload covered by two engines shows twice) — read one engine at a time.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, engine) (alatyr_workloads_covered{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}) / on (namespace) group_left sum by (namespace) (alatyr_workloads{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"})

panels.title: Per-namespace manifest census
panels.description: Distinct policy manifests per (namespace, engine). Deduped by (engine, ns, name) — a manifest producing many rules or mixing allow+deny counts once. Cluster-scoped policies (Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy, etc.) roll up under namespace=`_cluster`. Cheap detector for a GitOps sync that silently dropped a directory — a namespace whose count halved overnight is usually the story. Action, direction, coverage live on alatyr_rule_edges (Calico/Kyverno mix actions in one manifest, so keying by action would double-count).

panels.title: HTTP request duration p95 by path
Culprit policies by issue count
panels.description: One row per (namespace, type, engine, policy). Counts fan out each issue across its ingress + egress + node culprits; a policy cited on both sides of the same issue counts once. Powered by alatyr_issues_by_policy — disable via METRICS_ISSUE_POLICY_BREAKDOWN=false if cardinality bites.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, type, engine, policy_namespace, policy_name) (alatyr_issues_by_policy{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}) > 0

panels.title: Top 15 culprit policies
panels.description: Sum across all issue types + namespaces per policy. Answers 'which policy is causing the most breakage right now'.

panels.title: Culprit policy issue count over time
panels.description: Top 10 culprit policies over the dashboard time range. Useful for spotting new offenders vs steady-state noise.

panels.title: Rule edges by (namespace, engine, action, direction)
panels.description: Raw post-expansion rule count. One podSelector:{} manifest fans into src×dst edges; this counts every edge. Sum-safe across any label subset — use for total graph size, per-ns growth, or per-engine fan-out. A single row spiking overnight usually means someone widened a selector.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, engine, action, direction) (alatyr_rule_edges{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}) > 0

panels.title: Blanket detector — fan-out per coverage bucket
panels.description: Edge count vs distinct policies per (namespace, coverage) bucket, with ratio = avg fan-out per policy. High ratio in `namespace_wide` means one podSelector:{} policy inflating coverage — the failure mode where nobody wrote real policy but the graph looks covered. edges = sum(alatyr_rule_edges); policies = sum(alatyr_policy_coverage). Note: alatyr_policy_coverage is deduped per (policy, bucket) so summing across coverage buckets double-counts — read one bucket at a time.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, coverage) (alatyr_rule_edges{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"}) / sum by (namespace, coverage) (alatyr_policy_coverage{namespace=~"$namespace", namespace!~"$hide_infra"})

panels.title: Distinct policies per coverage bucket
panels.description: Raw alatyr_policy_coverage — one count per (policy, bucket). Deduped by (engine, ns, name, action, coverage, direction) so a manifest producing many rules with the same shape counts once per direction+action pair. Reads bucket-by-bucket: `namespace_wide` count is how many manifests are effectively blanket for that (ns, engine, action, direction). Do NOT sum across coverage or direction — a policy spanning multiple buckets appears once per bucket, so summing double-counts. For manifest-level totals use alatyr_policies instead.

list.label: Prometheus source
list.description: Prometheus datasource backing every panel on this dashboard.

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Filter to specific namespaces. Multi-select; defaults to All.

list.name: hide_infra
list.label: Hide infra namespaces
list.description: Regex of namespaces to exclude. Default drops control-plane noise. Set to '^$' to include everything.
